fig1: Fig. 1: Edge recovery against the number of samples, mean and one standard deviation over 20 graphs (D = 25, p = 0.1), with the values printed in the uGLAD paper as dotted hollow markers. The SGLCV curve reproduces the published one: the largest AUPR difference is 0.021, inside one standard deviation at every M. uGLAD run with the authors' code at its default settings does not: it is 0.040 to 0.076 below the published AUPR and, over the same graphs, differs from SGLCV by -0.004, -0.031 and -0.093 AUPR at M = 10, 25 and 50 (paired t = -0.5, -3.3, -4.9).
fig2: Fig. 2: (a) AUPR of uGLAD against AUPR of SGLCV on the same graph, so a point above the dashed line is a graph where uGLAD wins; uGLAD is above the line on 7, 2 and 1 of 20 graphs at M = 10, 25 and 50. (b) Number of edges in the learned graph, one marker per graph (vertical axis linear up to 1, logarithmic above). uGLAD returns an empty graph 11 and 12 times out of 20 at M = 25 and 50, and about 130 edges on average at M = 10, where the true graph has about 30.
fig3: Fig. 3: One recovered graph. It is the first of the 20 graphs at the largest M (M = 50, graph index 0); the rule was fixed before looking, so it is not a picked example. The true graph has 24 edges. SGLCV finds 2 of them and adds 2; uGLAD finds 0 and adds 0.
fig4: Fig. 4: Learning and inference KPIs on 20 test graphs per M, mean and one standard deviation, 1000 fresh test samples per graph, all methods compared in the raw units of the data. (a) Held-out negative log likelihood; the green curve is the true model, so no method can go below it. (b) Error of the exact conditional mean of each variable given all the others. At M = 50 the gap to the true model is 0.7 nats for SGLCV and 3.0 for uGLAD, but the prediction error differs by only 0.023 and 0.029.
fig5: Fig. 5: My implementation against the authors' code on the same 60 datasets with the same seeds. Each marker is one dataset. The two programs rank the node pairs alike: the correlation of AUPR is 1.00 and the mean absolute difference is 0.000 (largest 0.003). They are close but not identical, because the matrix square root is computed differently.
fig6: Fig. 6: The mathematics checked against independent references. (a) The alternating steps used inside uGLAD, run with three coupling weights on a D = 8 problem: the objective never rises (largest single-step increase 3e-15) and reaches the minimum found by a generic optimizer (L-BFGS). (b) The closed-form coefficient $-\Theta_{ij}/\Theta_{ii}$ of the conditional mean against the coefficient fitted by regression on 400000 simulated samples; the largest difference over 600 coefficients is 0.0053.
